Q: What is the difference between referring to something as an “object” versus a “constructor function” in JavaScript? A:

Object's prototype is the root prototype for most entities in JavaScript.

The items you list are all constructor functions, yes. 

typeof Array // 'function'

Invoking a constructor returns an object.

typeof (new Array()) // 'object'
typeof (new Date()) // 'object'

Q: Is assignment in Javascript template literals allowed? A:

Allowed by whom?

According to the grammar, it is: ECMA-262 6th Ed. §12.2.9, where template literals were first defined, specifies that an interpolation point is an Expression (a comma-operator expression), and the first level below that is an AssignmentExpression. Even if the grammar did not allow it directly, you could have wrapped the assignment in parentheses, which are also specified to contain an Expression.

Of course, things that are technically allowed by the grammar can still be discouraged by an official style guide, but for better or for worse, JavaScript has no such (unlike, say, Java); this is the land of “i have learned to use [semicolons], that's why there isn't one present”.

Would I personally ever write something like this? In the particular example presented in the question, assignment inside an interpolation point is pretty avoidable, so avoid it I would. It doesn’t help that in other programming languages, it is not always possible to reassign a value of a different type to a variable, or to reassign function parameters. But I can imagine cases where such a construct would have been much more useful and less dispensable (e.g. as a side channel to return partial results from a DSL interpreter), so it’s not something I would categorically forbid.

Q: Configure pyproject.toml for unittest and coverage A:

You should add this line to your file:

source = ["."]

That tells coverage to examine the whole tree for files to consider, even if they were never run.

Q: How to ask the user for a specific path to be used with open()? A:

It's pretty simple, just get the path from user:

subpath = raw_input("File path =  ")
print subpath
file = open(subpath + str(file_name), 'w+')
file.write(content)
file.close()

I think that's all you need.

Q: Time out error in deploying the process on weblogic server A:

This is just a warning. I get the same message when executing services that may take a long to finish. It doesn't create any actual problem in execution though, so you could just ignore it.

If you want to get rid of the warning (i wouldn't suggest to do that) you can open your server console and change the configuration. Specifically, for Weblogic (11g?), you should navigate to Environment Collapse NodeEnvironment> servers> {your_server}> Configuration> Overload> Max Stuck Thread Time and change from "600" to whatever you think. PS. I dont know to tell you if that change cause any problem of your server's execution! You should look after for any.
